newsitem.title: BURMA: U.N. official due to meet Burma's Suu Kyi.
newsitem.headline: U.N. official due to meet Burma's Suu Kyi.

text.p: A senior United Nations official was due to have talks with Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi in Rangoon on Friday but it was unclear if the military authorities would allow the meeting, U.N. officials said.

Assistant Secretary General Alvaro de Soto met foreign minister Ohn Gyaw on Thursday, the Myanmar News Agency reported. It did not say what they talked about but diplomats said they expected de Soto to discuss the human rights situation in Burma with Ohn Gyaw and other leaders in the military government.
U.N. officials were not sure if de Soto would be allowed to visit Suu Kyi, who has been under virtual house arrest since student demonstrations in December.
The government must approve visitors and allow them to pass through barricades that bar access to the street leading to the Nobel Peace laureate's home.
De Soto, who last visited Burma in August, arrived on Wednesday for a four-day official visit.
His last visit came only one month after Suu Kyi was released from six years of house arrest. He had been refused permission to see Suu Kyi on a previous visit.
De Soto has held several rounds of talks with Rangoon's military leaders on the human rights situation in Burma.

The State Law and Order Restoration Council has been accused by the United Nations and many Western governments of committing human rights abuses like summary executions, forced labour and arbitrary arrests of opposition politicians and supporters.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment on de Soto's visit.
